title: Reveal one strong reading, not the answer
statement: For an interpretive question, show a model answer only after a committed attempt, labelled as one strong reading with an invitation to disagree, never as the answer.
detail: The Grade 9 research brief combines a guarded-chatbot trial, a structured AI tutoring trial and a study of autonomy-supporting behaviour into an explicit hint ladder: a question back to the student, a pointer to a paragraph, two candidate sentences, then the model answer only after a committed attempt, labelled 'one strong reading', with an invitation to disagree. The Grade 9 strategy adopts the ladder for its argument tasks. Its order from general to specific matches the rule that help comes after a try, cues first; what it adds is how an interpretive item's answer is shown.
against: It is a proposal, neither built nor piloted, and in the trial it draws on, the hint-only arm erased most of the harm but did not beat the control group on the exam (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/learners-voice-guide.md`, line 164).

evidence.quote: Set the hint ladder as an explicit rule: (1) a question back to the student, (2) point to a paragraph, (3) narrow to two candidate sentences, (4) show the model answer only after a committed attempt, labeled "one strong reading," with an invitation to disagree.

**Hint ladder (from Bastani et al.):** a question back, then a pointer to a paragraph, then two candidate lines, then "one strong reading" only after a committed attempt, with an invitation to disagree.

citations.ref: Bastani, Bastani, Sungu, Ge, Kabakcı & Mariman 2025
